facts.fact: Countdown to 2030's analysis with the health ministry's DPRS and DSME states that the overall quality score of health facility data in DHIS2 fell from 71% in 2019 to 63% in 2024, chiefly because strikes in health facilities between 2022 and 2024 disrupted the regular transmission of data into DHIS2; it gives the share of districts with reporting completeness of 90% or more for antenatal care and deliveries as 31% in 2019 and 57% in 2024, while describing that share as having fallen.

The same analysis states that for the years after 2019 the missing of district vaccination coverage targets is explained largely by data being unavailable in more than 30% of districts, and that the gap between Penta3 coverage from DHIS2 and from the DHS survey widened from 5% in 2019 to nearly 15% in 2023, which it puts down to variable data quality in DHIS2.

systems.tiers: health facility data analysed by district; weak reporting by the private sector into the platform; tiers not stated

note: The document gives no figure for facilities entering their own reports; its completeness figures are shares of districts, and the two it prints (31% in 2019, 57% in 2024) contradict the fall it describes.
